concept.title: Avoid Phishing Scams
concept.shortdesc: The warning signs for phishing, prevention strategies, common campus scams, and procedures for reporting suspicious messages.

conbody.p: Phishing attacks across the NC State community arrive through email, text messages, shared Google Docs, and calendar invites. Attackers often impersonate trusted university offices or businesses to lure users into clicking harmful links or entering credentials on fake login pages.

section.title: Common Campus Phishing Lures
section.p: Scammers frequently tailor messages to target NC State students, faculty, and staff using familiar university themes:

ul.li: Fake university account warnings: Messages claiming your Unity account or email storage will be deactivated unless you verify your login immediately.
Payroll and pension review scams: Emails impersonating human resources or benefits offices asking you to review salary, tax, or retirement documents.
Fraudulent student job offers: Unsolicited emails advertising high-paying, flexible campus or remote jobs that ask for personal or banking information.

section.title: Three Core Phishing Prevention Habits
section.p: To protect yourself and university systems across all campus roles, follow NC State OIT's three core prevention habits:

ul.li: Be suspicious: Treat any unsolicited request for login credentials, financial details, or personal contact information with caution.
Take your time: Inspect links before clicking and verify that official NC State login URLs begin with shib.ncsu.edu (for Shibboleth) or login.microsoftonline.com (for Entra ID).
Ask for help: Report suspected phishing messages through Gmail's built-in reporting feature and the NC State OIT Help Desk.
